messages:
rachel: Quick design sync 1 we need to decide how sample tiles appear in the first-run home: compact grid (4 tiles) vs expanded cards (2 tiles with screenshots). Mobile and accessibility concerns in play. Thoughts?

drew: Compact grid shows more choices but screenshots get tiny. Expanded cards let us show 1-line descriptions and clearer CTAs. My vote: expanded on desktop, compact on small widths.

mohit: Perf note: expanded cards load larger images which hurts initial paint. Could lazy-load screenshots after first interaction. Also consider using SVG placeholders.

anya: From research, new users prefer clarity over choice. They click a single prominent example more often. Suggest default expanded on first-run, with an inline "More examples" compact grid below.

rachel: Good. Accessibility: ensure each tile has an explicit aria-label like `Sample: Chat assistant (Python)` and the CTA is a real button, not just a link. Tab order should go CTA first, then details.

a11y-bot: a11y-check: color contrast for the pill labels fails at 12px. Use >=13px semibold or adjust background. Also ensure keyboard users can activate sample preview with Enter/Space.

drew: Copy tweak: current hero CTA reads "Start with a sample project" (long). Suggest "Try a sample" on small screens and "Try a sample project" on desktop.

mohit: Implementation plan: load low-res blurred image in src, swap to high-res when card enters viewport or CTA gets focus. That should balance perf and clarity.

anya: UX microcopy for the preview modal: header = sample name, subhead = one-line intent (e.g., "Q&A demo for docs"), CTA = "Run demo" + small footnote: "No code uploaded." Keep privacy messaging clear.

rachel: Action items: 1) Drew update comps for expanded + secondary grid 2) Mohit add lazy-load spec + placeholder assets 3) Anya craft modal microcopy and aria-label list 4) A11y-bot create a tiny contrast token checklist. I'll put these into the onboarding epic and loop in product marketing for localized strings. Thanks all :sparkles:
